newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Highlights of Indonesia's 1997/98 state budget.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Indonesia's 1997/98 state budget.

text.p: President Suharto unveiled Indonesia's 1997/98 state budget in parliament on Monday effective from April 1. Following are the highlights:
-- The budget will expand over 1996/97 by 11.6 percent to 101.09 trillion rupiah. It's the first time the state budget had exceeded 100 trillion rupiah
-- Non-oil/gas revenue projected to increase by 14.2 percent to 73.19 trillion rupiah from 64.08 trillion rupiah
-- Oil/gas revenue expected to rise 5.3 percent to 14.87 trillion rupiah from 14.12 trillion rupiah
-- Current account deficit expected to rise to $9.789 billion from an expected $8.823 billion in 1996/97
-- Inflation in 1996 6.47 percent, compared with 8.64 percent in 1995 and 9.2 percent in 1994. Seen 6.0 percent in 1997/98
-- Price of crude oil set at $16.50/barrel, unchanged from 1996/97
-- Foreign exchange reserves expected to rise to $20 billion
-- Debt service ratio expected to be 31.2 percent, compared with an estimated 31.7 percent in 1996/97
-- Broad M-2 money supply forecast to rise 18 percent to 323.6 trillion rupiah; narrow M-1 money expected to rise 16 percent to 71.55 trillion rupiah
-- Credit seen expanding 17.0 percent to 331.93 trillion rupiah, against an expected 16 percent rise to 276.45 trillion rupiah in the 1996/97
-- Government has no plans to raise tax rates
